reading.body:
Adam Smith's AI record shows $27,000 in committee contributions from Google, Microsoft, Intel, Amazon, and Palantir over eighteen months, alongside three AI-related bills he cosponsored and four recorded votes.

The money is steady and comes from the largest AI and cloud companies. Microsoft gave twice, Amazon twice, Google twice, Intel once, Palantir once. The contributions run from February 2025 through July 2026 with no long gap. The bills he cosponsored cover facial recognition, tax enforcement technology, and immigration enforcement, which are three different parts of the AI policy space rather than one specialty.

What the data does not show is causation. The page states plainly that events are placed in date order and that placement is not a claim one event caused another. A contribution and a vote can sit near each other on a timeline without being connected. The votes listed are on bills the data does not name beyond their numbers, so a reader cannot tell from this page alone whether any of them concerned AI directly.

For AI specifically, the pattern matters because the companies giving here are the same companies building and operating the data centers that AI depends on. Their political committees are spending on members who sit on committees that touch technology and enforcement. That is a fact about where money goes, not proof of what it buys. The record covers one member and fifteen events, which is enough to see a pattern and not enough to explain it.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Adam Smith: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 15 events, and 1 news stories that name them.
